justification: Schedules the existing citation checker nightly with --apply in data-watch. It writes only citation_status, citation_source_path and citation_checked_at, only onto the chapter PDF in force. The page shows a clause number only when 'proven', so a changed verdict can hide or show a clause number; nothing else changes.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-10-12: served council rules with a verdict were last judged 2026-10-02 (citation_checked_at max); 962 council rules have none -- 408 Ashfield rows restored 2026-10-10 and 554 Inner West LEP rows with no chapter (not DCP, outside this checker). Dry run: 19,627 judged, 440 to change.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The checker's docstring said it ran nightly; no workflow, cron or worker scheduled it, and I repeated the claim to the user before checking.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new code: one step in the existing nightly data-watch workflow, which already holds the database and R2 secrets and raises a single reused issue on failure.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The dry run prints the verdict counts and the number to write; the nightly step's outcome is in data-watch's FAILED list, so a crash or a missing secret raises the alarm issue.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before this, nothing ran: the newest citation_checked_at was 2026-10-02 and 408 restored Ashfield rules had no verdict. The dry run on 2026-10-12 judged 19,627 rules with exit 0.

functions.name: main
functions.input: DATABASE_URL and R2 secrets from the workflow, and --apply
functions.output: Verdict counts printed; changed verdicts written in batches, guarded to the chapter PDF still in force
functions.if_none: A missing PDF is the verdict no_source, not a crash; a missing citation_source_path column refuses to write.

values.what: council rules judged by the dry run / verdicts that would change
values.if_missing: A database or R2 failure exits non-zero and raises the data-watch alarm.

queries.purpose: Write each changed verdict only onto the chapter PDF still in force.
queries.where_clause: WHERE p.id = v.id AND p.is_current AND EXISTS (dcp_chapter_registry reg WHERE reg.is_active AND reg.council = p.source_council AND reg.chapter_key = p.source_chapter_key AND reg.r2_current_path IS NOT DISTINCT FROM v.src)

break_it.scenario: A chapter is republished while the nightly job is writing verdicts for it.
break_it.what_happens: An old verdict could land on the new chapter's rows and show an unproven clause number.
break_it.how: The UPDATE only writes where the registry's current PDF path equals the PDF the verdict was judged on.

break_it.scenario: The R2 secrets are missing or wrong on the runner.
break_it.what_happens: Every chapter would be judged no_source and its clause numbers hidden.
break_it.how: A missing secret raises KeyError before any write (os.environ[...]), so the step fails and the alarm issue opens; no verdict is written.

break_it.scenario: Writing each changed verdict hits a row whose chapter is inactive.
break_it.what_happens: A verdict could be written for a chapter that is no longer served.
break_it.how: The guard requires reg.is_active; inactive chapters are skipped.

post_merge.db_reset: Nightly from now on (verdict columns only). Today's 440 changes are written only with the user's yes.
post_merge.secrets: No new secrets; reuses DATABASE_URL and R2_* already in data-watch.
post_merge.manual_verify: Dry run 2026-10-12: exit 0, 19,627 judged, 440 to write.
